full_judgment: 21. In Abdul Hamid vs Abbas Bhai A Hossain, 14 DLR (SC) 24, two agreements were executed for sale of a plot-under the first agreement Rs.2000 was paid as earnest money to the vendor and it was agreed that the balance of Rs 13750 would be paid within two months from the date of agreement on the vendor's obtaining certificate from Income- Tax-Authorities, certificate from the Rent Controller for making out clear title. It was stipulated in second agreement that the vendee would pay Rs. 3750 out of the balance amount within one week and in-case of his failure to pay Rs. 10,000 within two months, the vendor would grant him 18 months extension from the date of agreement within which period the vendee was to be entitled at any time to pay the balance Rs. 10,000 and obtain deed. The possession of the land was given to the vendee as per agreement. On 4th September, 1950 the vendor had notified the vendee that he had obtained necessary permissions and gave him 10 days time to complete the transaction. The vendor then rescinded the contract. In the facts of the given case, the issue before the Supreme Court that arose was; whether 'the purported rescission of the contract by the defendant-respondent based on any improper conduct on the part of the appellant, prior to the 4th September, 1950 when he attempted to fix a period of ten days for the performance. The court noticed the views taken by the Judicial Committee in Jamshed Khodaram Irani and two other English decisions and answered the question in the negative observing "The answer must clearly be in the negative, till then, the vendor was not in a position to say that he had completed his own part .of the contract and, consequently, he could not have charged the plaintiff appellant with laches or dilatoriness in offering to perform. The appellant was perfectly within his' right insisting before that date he could not be called upon to pay the purchase-price till the respondent had armed himself with the necessary certificate without which registration was not possible. .......... 'The principle; that if time is not originally made of the essence of a contract for sale of land, one of the parties is not entitled afterwards, by notice, to make it of the essence, unless there has been some default or unreasonable delay by the other party "
